wa33_fit.notes: The WA33 (2nd gen) uses a single rectifier tube on an octal socket. Stock tube is 5U4G; 274B is the marketed upgrade and fits the same octal socket. The WA33 product description names the 274B but the default-tube spec sheet lists 5U4G. The 274B draws 2 A filament vs the 5U4G's 3 A, so the filament winding is not stressed. Critical difference: 274B allows only 4 uF first capacitor (vs 40 uF for 5U4G) and 150 mA max DC output (vs 225 mA for 5U4G). 300B does NOT fit this amplifier. 274A (UX4 base) does NOT fit the WA33 octal socket.

warnings: Arcing: the WE 274B long plate sparks when the first power-supply capacitor exceeds 4 uF; this forced Western Electric to limit the design to 4 uF and prevented wide adoption

First capacitor limit: 4 uF max for NOS WE 274B; 8 uF max for Sophia rigid/mesh plate; modern Sophia Aqua line and EML at low voltage allow higher values; always verify the amplifier's first capacitor before installing a 274B
Current limit: 274B max DC output is 150 mA (cap input) vs 225 mA for 5U4G; insufficient for high-current amplifiers
Filament: 5 V / 2 A directly heated; the 5U4G draws 3 A, so a 5U4G-rated transformer winding can power a 274B but not vice versa
Counterfeit NOS: vintage WE 274B tubes sell for $1500-5000+; counterfeits and relabeled tubes exist in the market
Socket: 274A uses a UX4 (4-pin) base and will NOT fit the WA33's octal 274B/5U4G socket
Compatibility: Sophia Aqua II 274B may cause premature failure in some amplifiers and DACs (Decware SE84UFO, some Lampizator DACs); Aqua III is the safer choice
Mesh plate current limits: mesh plate 274B variants have stricter current and capacitor limits than solid plate versions

sonic_lore.summary: Jeff Day (Positive Feedback) calls the 274B his favorite rectifier 'by leaps and bounds,' praising its holographic imaging, natural tonality, and spectacular soundstaging. NOS WE 274B tubes are endangered and command $1500-5000 on the used market.

Jeff Day's Positive Feedback review describes the Aqua II as having 'a natural tonal balance, a huge sense of recorded acoustic, clearly articulated tone color, a vivid sense of imaging presence, and excellent dynamics.' It won the 2023 Positive Feedback Writers' Choice Award.

Sophia Electric describes the Aqua III as offering 'nearly identical sonic performance to the Mark II' while being 'virtually foolproof for a wide range of applications.' It is the recommended choice for 300B amplifiers, Decware amplifiers, and Lampizator DACs.

EML describes the 274B as producing 'improved sound compared to lower impedance rectifier tubes such as 5U4G' with less mechanical hum and better resolution. EML was the first company to re-introduce the 274 tube, in 2001.

wa33_fit.notes: The WA33 2nd generation uses four 2A3 output tubes as a matched quad in a fully balanced push-pull class-A amplifier. 300B tubes must not be substituted; use only compatible 2A3-family tubes confirmed for heater current, bias, socket, and clearance.

sonic_lore.summary: Classic American NOS 2A3s are treated as the tone benchmark: saturated, midrange-rich, and natural at headphone levels. The appeal is texture and intimacy more than brute force.
The saved Glow in the Dark Audio comparison singles out an early-2000s Sovtek Reflektor as its preferred example. In WA33 terms it is the pragmatic modern choice to compare against boutique tubes.
Sophia-style mesh/globe 2A3 lore emphasizes atmosphere and bloom. Treat it as a delicacy-first tube and verify dissipation and handling before use.

JJ 2A3-40 is best understood as a robust high-dissipation variant rather than a strict vintage clone. It can sound controlled and powerful, but compatibility matters more than its headline 40 W rating.
Psvane-style audiophile 2A3s are usually chosen for polish and image density. They should be purchased from a reliable source because model naming and regional lines vary.

wa33_fit.notes: The Woo Audio WA33 (2nd gen) Standard Edition uses one 5U4G as the stock rectifier. The 274B is the common upgrade path (Takatsuki TA-274B, Sophia Aqua III 274B, Psvane WE274B sold by Woo Audio). The 5U4G and 274B are NOT interchangeable without the amplifier being designed for both (different filament current: 3 A vs 2 A). The 5U4GB is NOT a safe substitute for the 5U4G (different internal resistance, higher output voltage). 300B does not fit this amplifier.

warnings: Filament fragility: the directly heated filament draws 3 A at 5 V; over-voltage or physical shock can break it.
Do not substitute 5U4GB for 5U4G: the GB has lower internal resistance and produces higher rectified voltage; the G can be damaged if substituted for a GB.
Input capacitor must not exceed 40 µF; exceeding this causes high charge-current peaks, tube damage, and hum radiation.
Minimum transformer winding resistance ~170-230 Ω required for capacitor-input filter; add series resistors if too low.
Arcing: operating beyond PIV (1550 V) or with excessive input capacitance can cause internal arcing (white spark at switch-on).
274B filament current (2 A) differs from 5U4G (3 A); the amplifier must be designed for the correct current.
Counterfeit mesh-plate 5U4G tubes exist; buy from reputable dealers.
300B does not fit the WA33; only 2A3, 6C45, 5U4G, and 274B families apply.

sonic_lore.summary: The EML mesh-plate 5U4G is a slow-start tube that enables ultra-low-ripple operation when used with a choke-input filter, producing a quiet, smooth power supply. Its mesh construction and protective heater stabilization are designed for long life and low hum-field radiation.

NOS RCA 5U4G tubes are the classic stock rectifier in many vintage and modern tube amplifiers, valued for their warm, smooth character. They are directly heated and provide gradual B+ rise due to the filament warm-up time.

sonic_lore.model: 274B upgrade (Takatsuki TA-274B / Sophia Aqua III / Psvane WE274B)

Frank's tube archive and its altanatubes mirror list the 6S45PE as a “Soviet” brand tube dated approximately 1977, classified as a triode (type code “t”).

wa33_fit.notes: The Woo Audio WA33 (2nd generation) uses four 6C45 tubes as the driver stage in a fully balanced Class-A push-pull configuration, paired with four 2A3 power tubes and one 5U4G rectifier (5U3C is an equivalent designation). The 6C45 is the stock driver for both the Standard and Elite Editions. The Western Electric 417A, Raytheon 5842, and GEC CV3789 can be substituted as driver upgrades but require a custom 31 mm adapter; Woo Audio sells these as factory-matched tube-plus-adapter sets and states the tube and adapter must not be separated. A standard 300B (5 V filament) does NOT fit the WA33; only the EML 300B-2.5 (2.5 V filament) has been confirmed compatible by Jack Woo. The WA33 is self-biasing with compatible tubes; Woo provides a tube-compatibility chart (Google Sheets, login-gated).

warnings: High microphonics — the very high transconductance and small electrode structure make the 6C45 mechanically sensitive to vibration; socket damping and careful placement matter in audio service
Heater pins run warm — the 0.44 A heater at 6.3 V dissipates about 2.8 W and can heat the noval pins; ensure good socket contact
Noise at low signal levels — high-gm triodes tend to be noisier than low-gm types; select low-noise specimens for driver stages
Burn-in — 50–100 hours of burn-in is commonly recommended before final sonic judgement
WE 417A / 5842 / CV3789 adapter — these substitutes require a custom 31 mm adapter to fit the 6C45 noval socket; tube and adapter are factory matched and must not be separated
300B does NOT fit — the standard 300B has a 5 V filament and is electrically incompatible; only the 2.5 V EML 300B-2.5 variant has been confirmed WA33-compatible by Jack Woo

Datasheet image-only — the primary Russian 6S45P-E datasheet in Frank's archive is a scanned image with no extractable text; secondary sources (radiomuseum.org) provide the filament and base data in HTML

sonic_lore.model: WA33 Elite Edition with EH 6C45Pi drivers
sonic_lore.summary: The WA33 Elite Edition with Electro-Harmonix 6C45Pi drivers is described as neutral and transparent rather than lush or overly warm, combining solid-state-like speed and slam with a smooth, non-harsh top end. Bass is deep and textured, the soundstage is holographic and wide with exceptional depth, and there is generous air around each instrument.

NOS Soviet 6S45P-E tubes are generally regarded as more detailed and resolving than the current Electro-Harmonix production, with a cleaner, faster presentation, but they are also more microphonic and harder to match into quiet quads. Direct sonic testimony from a saved source is limited; most owner reports come from head-fi and forum.headphones.com threads that are JavaScript-rendered and could not be fetched as text.

Woo Audio positions the Western Electric 417A, Raytheon 5842, and GEC CV3789 as premium NOS driver upgrades that elevate the already exceptional WA33 to jaw-dropping sonic performance via a custom 31 mm 417A-to-6C45 adapter. These are the only documented driver substitutes for the 6C45 in the WA33, sold as factory-matched tube-plus-adapter sets.
